statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Since the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen NQ has held a 40.75-point band, 29,449.50 to 29,490.25, trading near 29,458.75 and up 0.03%. Monday's Nasdaq-100 cash session closed at 29,127.16, down 241.28 points or 0.82%, after gapping 1.63% below the 29,368.44 previous close to open at 28,890.93, bottoming at 28,867.67 and recovering 417 points to 29,285.50. The decline was rotational rather than index-wide: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.9% while software and communication services rose. VIX closed at 17.10, up 7.95%, but well below its 18.17 session high. Stress remains high at 65 on a 10-year Treasury yield that touched 5.01% for the first time since October 2023 before reversing, WTI near $102.19 with the Saudi East-West pipeline still shut, and a contested Federal Reserve decision on 16 September.
recommendation: Tail at 15 sits in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Three independent mean-reversion events occurred on Monday: the cash index recovered 417 points off its low, the 10-year yield's move above 5% was erased as buyers emerged, and crude trimmed gains of up to 5%. That is the opposite of a price path that denies retracement. The danger window is retained at 13:00 to 15:00 UTC on 15 September, covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where a second consecutive gap open after a chip-led de-rating is the specific structure that would matter. Conditional Tail peaks at 24 there, the top of the watch band, without reaching the block threshold. Stress stays high because the rates, oil and policy backdrop can still produce a large but recoverable drawdown.
headline: Globex reopens quietly with NQ near 29,458.75 in a 40-point band after a rotational Monday in which the Nasdaq-100 recovered 417 points off its low, the 10-year's 5% breach was rejected and crude trimmed a 5% spike; Tail holds at 15 in the low band while Stress stays high at 65
body:
The current hour carries genuine observed evidence rather than an evidence gap. CME equity index futures reopened at 22:00 UTC and NQ has held a band only 40.75 points wide, from 29,449.50 to 29,490.25, trading near 29,458.75 and up 0.03% on volume of roughly 4,400 contracts. Two independent quote sources agree on the level. An orderly, narrow reopen is the most direct available evidence against a pathological price path.

Monday resolved as a two-sided session. The Nasdaq-100 cash index gapped 1.63% below the 29,368.44 previous close to open at 28,890.93, bottomed at 28,867.67, rallied 417 points to 29,285.50 and closed at 29,127.16, down 0.82%. The S&P 500 fell 0.48% and the Dow 0.29%. Both the decline and the recovery retraced inside the range, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines Tail risk.

The composition matters more than the index move. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.9%, with Nvidia down 3.37%, Intel down 5.59%, Micron down about 6% and SK Hynix down 7%, after weekend essays from the Anthropic and OpenAI chief executives argued for slowing the pace of AI capability improvement. Against that, latest-session context shows Alphabet up 3.22%, Meta up 2.71% and Microsoft up 1.97%, with software and communication services higher. A decline concentrated in one industry and offset elsewhere in the index is a rotation. Under the governing framework, conflicting breadth of this kind raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than mechanically raising Tail.

The macro backdrop is genuinely heavy and is the reason Stress stays at 65 in the high band. The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.00% on Monday for the first time since October 2023, reaching about 5.01%, within a basis point of its highest level since 2002, before the move was erased as buyers emerged. H.15 for 11 September shows the 2-year at 4.63%, the 10-year at 4.96% and the 30-year at 5.35%. WTI trades near $102.19, up about 1.3%, after an intraday spike toward $105, and Brent reached about $109 before trimming gains. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, a 7 million barrel per day route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, has been shut since 11 September after drone attacks launched from Iraq, with no announced restart timeline. VIX closed at 17.10, up 7.95% but below its 18.17 session high and still far from a stress regime.

Three of these amplifiers reversed within the same session rather than compounding. That pattern is inconsistent with the aligned, unresolved amplifier stack that would justify a Tail reading in the elevated band, so Tail eases to 15 and the low-band mapping is retained.

Forward risk is concentrated in two places. The near one is Tuesday's US cash open at 13:30 UTC, where a second consecutive gap open after a chip-led de-rating is the credible path-pathology scenario; the danger window covers 13:00 to 15:00 UTC and conditional Tail peaks at 24, the top of the watch band. The 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC carries more weight than usual with the long end at these levels. The larger event, the Federal Reserve decision at 18:00 UTC on 16 September with projections and a press conference, falls outside this 24-hour horizon. It is structurally multi-stage and contested: a 25 basis point hike, which would be the first since 2023, is priced as more likely than not, but venue-to-venue dispersion is wide. Under the governing framework that dispersion raises Stress and affects Confidence rather than raising Tail before anything is observed.

Shared cross-asset context collected at 22:47 UTC was healthy apart from its calendar section, which was unavailable; the seven-day calendar below was verified independently. That context is delayed, latest-session information and was used only for breadth, megacap and semiconductor tone, never as live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail opened the window at 20, held a 19 to 21 plateau through the Asian session, rose to a 26 peak during the European morning chip-led decline, eased, repeated 26 at the US cash open, then decayed steadily through the afternoon to 15 by the Globex reopen as the opening gap was recovered. Stress fell from a 79 peak to 65 and Confidence held between 80 and 89. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all concentrated in the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band through the remainder of the Asian session, with small uplifts at the Tokyo cash open and the Hong Kong and mainland opens, then eases to an overnight floor of 15. It rises to 18 for the European opening auction, enters the watch band at 20 from 12:00 UTC ahead of the Empire State survey, and peaks at 24 across the 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It returns to the lower watch band in the midday lull, steps up to 22 for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, holds at 21 into the final cash hour before Federal Reserve decision day, then falls to 17 during the CME maintenance halt and 18 at the Globex reopen. No hour in the window reaches the block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the high band throughout, peaking at 74 at the cash open, and Confidence decays from 89 to 77 with forecast distance.
